name: Hypomaturation-Hypoplastic Amelogenesis Imperfecta with Taurodontism
aliases: AI with hypomaturation and hypoplastic defects

criteria.description: Presence of enamel with abnormal mineralization leading to mottled, opaque, or discolored enamel
Defective enamel matrix formation resulting in thin or pitted enamel
Enlarged pulp chambers with apically displaced furcation of molar teeth
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Radiographic evidence of reduced enamel thickness and altered radiodensity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both hypomaturation and hypoplastic enamel defects plus taurodontism on radiographic examination
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Generalized enamel hypomaturation with mottled opaque discoloration
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic enamel appearance differentiates from other AI types

pathognomonic.symptomName: Enamel hypoplasia presenting as thin, pitted, or rough enamel surfaces
searchTerms: thin, pitted, or rough enamel surfaces
enamel with pits or rough texture

pathognomonic.symptomName: Taurodontism of molar teeth with enlarged pulp chambers
pathognomonic.notes: Detected radiographically, hallmark of this AI subtype

common.symptomName: Increased dental sensitivity to thermal and mechanical stimuli
searchTerms: teeth sensitive to touch and temperature
pain from mechanical and thermal stimuli

common.symptomName: Accelerated enamel wear leading to short clinical crowns
searchTerms: fast enamel loss causing short teeth
worn down teeth with short crowns

common.notes: Due to enamel defects and underlying dentin exposure

common.symptomName: Malocclusion secondary to abnormal tooth morphology

occasional.notes: Due to enamel defects and plaque accumulation

searchTerms: teeth hurt when eating acid foods

occasional.symptomName: Mild facial asymmetry related to dental abnormalities
searchTerms: unequal facial features related to teeth

rare.symptomName: Pulp necrosis without obvious caries or trauma
Enamel fracture leading to tooth loss
searchTerms: tooth enamel damage causing tooth loss

laboratory: Normal serum calcium and phosphate levels
imaging: Panoramic radiographs showing thin enamel layer
Taurodontism with enlarged pulp chambers on molars
Reduced enamel radiodensity compared to dentin
genetic: Inheritance patterns may be autosomal dominant or recessive
other: Clinical dental examination revealing enamel defects
Family history consistent with hereditary enamel defects

distinguishingFeatures: Normal pulp chamber size without taurodontism
Defects primarily in dentin rather than enamel

redFlags: Severe enamel breakdown leading to rapid tooth loss
Persistent dental sensitivity unresponsive to standard care
Early onset of dental abscesses without caries or trauma
references: Witkop CJ Jr. Amelogenesis imperfecta, dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentin dysplasia revisited: problems in classification. J Oral Pathol. 1988;17(9-10):547-53.
Kim JW, Simmer JP. Hereditary dentin defects. J Dent Res. 2007;86(5):392-9.
Hart PS, Hart TC. Genetic studies of amelogenesis imperfecta: a review. Cells Tissues Organs. 2007;186(1):13-23.
